Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The New Zealand Women players stride out to the middle. Followed by Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma who walk out to open for India Women. Frances Mackay to start with the new ball.
... The Run Chase ...

Right then! India Women have a daunting task in front of them as they need 192 runs to win off 20 overs if they are to get their first win of the tour. With Smriti Mandhana coming back into the side, they will believe that they can achieve the required runs but it's going to be really difficult. All New Zealand Women now need is a couple of wickets early in the Powerplay to put their opponents under immense pressure. The run chase is coming up soon.

India Women will be hugely disappointed with that bowling effort. They have been at fault of leaking runs in the death overs but their bowlers were put under the pump today right from the start. Meghna Singh was wayward and got hit all around the park. Renuka Singh though bowled well but still found it difficult to stem the flow of runs. The spinners were brought on to control the middle overs but apart from Rajeshwari Gayakwad, no one else managed to do that. Everyone received a tap and Pooja Vastrakar was given just the solitary over. Renuka Singh was the pick of the bowlers as she got two important wickets and didn't concede too many runs.

It's been an absolutely blistering 20 overs of batting from New Zealand Women! They have notched up 191 runs off just 20 overs and have given their opponents a mountain to climb. Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates did open the batting today and the two went ballistic from the start as they added von 53 runs for the first-wicket partnership. Neither could get to a half-century but Amy Satterthwaite and Amelia Kerr didn't let the solid foundation laid at the start go to waste. Satterthwaite did fall but once again it was Amelia Kerr with a big innings. She ended with 68 runs off just 33 balls and has propelled her team to a monstrous total.
FOUR! Kerr manages to end the innings on a high! Full length, outside off. Kerr carves it through covers to bag a boundary. New Zealand Women end their innings at 191/5.
Another one worked to long on for a brace.
Full and on off. Kerr drills it down to long on for a brace.
SIX! BANG! Full and on leg. Kerr smokes it over the square leg fence for a biggie.
A single as this worked to point.
OUT! TIMBER! A wicket to start the final over with. Tossed up, full and on the stumps. Lauren Down tries to sweep it away but misses. The ball goes through to shatter the stumps.
FOUR! Full and on middle. Amelia Kerr whips it across the line for a boundary.
Played through mid off for one.
A dot now, as this is defended out.
FOUR! Short and outside off. Down cruches it through point for a boundary.
Three wides! Full and down leg. Lauren Down looks to flick but misses. The keeper also misses and they take two runs as well.
Who will bowl the final over? It's going to be Deepti Sharma (3-0-34-0).
Lauren Down walks in to bat now.

OUT! TIMBER! Renuka Singh gets her second wicket. It is tossed up and on leg. Frances Mackay gets inside the line and looks to scoop it over the keeper's head but fails to get any bat on it. The balll goes through and clips the bails on it's way.
Floated, full and off. Kerr works it towards mid on for a single. FIFTY for Kerr.
Renuka Singh (3-0-20-1) to bowl the 19th over.

Everyone's bamboozled at the moment! Slowed up, on a length and around off. Frances Mackay shuffles right across her stumps and looks to paddle it fine. The ball comes off her gloves and misses the off pole by a whisker. Mackay also falls over and has a laugh about it.
Frances Mackay punches it to mid off.
Fuller on the stumps. Amelia Kerr flicks it to the leg side for one more.
Full, on middle and leg. Frances Mackay flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and on off. Kerr drills it down the ground for one.
FOUR! Amelia Kerr is not stopping here. Short and on off. Amelia Kerr hangs back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
On leg. Kerr clips it to mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries. Tossed up, full, on middle and leg. Amelia Kerr gets low and sweeps it through mid-wicket to find another boundary.
FOUR! Kerr motoring along really well. Fuller, on off. Kerr gets low and slog sweeps it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
On the stumps. Frances Mackay eases it to cover with soft hands. The fielder collects the ball and scores a direct-hit at the striker's end. The ball deflects out and they take one.
Floated, full and on off. Frances Mackay defends it out.
Safe! Slightly short and on off. Amelia Kerr pulls it to deep mid-wicket. The ball meets the fielder on a bounce. One taken.
Full and on off. Amelia Kerr flicks it through mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and on off. Frances Mackay reverse-sweeps it to point for one.
On the stumps. Frances Mackay blocks it out.
Touch short and outside off. Amelia Kerr helps it to third man for one.
A single as this is helped to mid off.
Tossed up, full and on off. Frances Mackay defends it out.
Full and on leg. Frances Mackay flicks it to mid-wicket for one.

Meghna Singh gets her into an awkward position while looking to throw the ball and she slips. She seems to have hurt her ankle a bit. The physio is on the field and Singh is now being carried out for further assessment.
Tossed up, full and outside off. Frances Mackay looks to defend it out but gets pinged on the pads. Rana appeals but the umpire is unmoved.
Around middle and leg. Frances Mackay works it out to safety.
Full, on middle and leg. Kerr works it to square leg for one.
WIDE! Tossed up, down leg. Kerr looks to chase it but misses. Wide called.
Full and on leg. Frances Mackay glances it to fine leg for one.
On off, Mackay blocks it out.
Sneh Rana (1-0-10-0) is back on.
FOUR! Nicely played. Amelia Kerr races away to 30. Full length and on off. Amelia Kerr whips across the line through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Fuller, on leg. Frances Mackay flicks it to mid-wicket for one.
Frances Mackay is in at number 5.

OUT! TIMBER! Meghna Singh picks up her first wicket of the game. Singh fires in a full-lneght delivery, on the stumps. The ball does not bounce much off deck. Amy Satterthwaite stays inside the crease and tires to heave it across the line but misses. It goes through to shatter the stumps.
FOUR! Runs are coming in thick and fast for New Zealand Women. A short ball, outside off. Amy Satterthwaite stands tall andcuts it through point for a boundary.
FOUR! What a shot! A short ball, on off. Amy Satterthwaite stays inside the crease and crunches it through mid-wicket. Boundary.
Back of a length, on off. Amy Satterthwaite stays back and looks to pull it away but misses.
Meghna Singh (3-0-32-0) is back on.
Another single as this is eased into mid on.
Fuller, on leg. Kerr nudges it to mid-wicket for one.
A single as this is worked to long off.

Misfield and four! India haven't been up to the mark in the field. A full-length ball, on off. Amy Satterthwaite drills it down the ground to long. The fielder in the deep misses and the ball runs into the ropes.
SIX! Back-to-back maximums. Full, on middle and leg. Amy Satterthwaite advances down the track and flicks it over the mid-wicket fence.
SIX! All the way! Floated, full, on middle and off. Amy Satterthwaite comes down the track and smokes it over the mid-wicket fence for a maximum.
Fuller, on off. Amelia Kerr defends it to point.
FOUR! She goes again! Floated, full and outside off. Amelia Kerr gets across the line and helps it over the short fine leg fielder for a boundary.
FOUR! Nicely played. Tossed up, full and outside off. Amelia Kerr gets across the line and scoops it over short fine leg for a boundary.
On middle and off, blocked out.
Full and on leg. Amy Satterthwaite clips it to square leg for one.
On the pads, Kerr clips it through mid-wicket for a single.
Sneh Rana to roll her arm now.
Full length, on off. Amy Satterthwaite works it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Short ball, on off. Amelia Kerr pulls it to long on for a single.
Tossed up, full and on off. Kerr punches it to mid off.
Full and on off. Amy Satterthwaite sweeps it to the leg side for one.
Around off, pushed to single for one more.
Short and outside off. Amy Satterthwaite cuts it to covers for one.
FOUR! Down the leg side, Amelia Kerr looks to sweep it away fine but gets a top edge. There is no one there at the fine leg fence and Kerr will pick up a boundary.
On a length, slower through the air and turning in. Satterthwaite tucks it away through mid-wicket for a single.
Nicely tossed up again, outside off. Satterthwaite looks to fetch it and broom it away but the ball sneaks under her blade.
Tossed up, full and on off. Amy Satterthwaite pushes it out on the off side.
Amy Satterthwaite is the new batter in.

OUT! STUMPED! This is some really fine glove work from Richa Ghosh. Tossed up, on off. Suzie Bates dances down the track but overruns it a bit. Bates ends up yorking herself and gets a bottom edge back to the keeper. Ghosh is really quick to collect the ball and whips off the bails before Bates is able to get back. The umpire doesn't even need a replay and Rajeshwari Gayakwad has some redemption for the dropped catch.
Commentary.Howout: st Richa Ghosh b Rajeshwari Gayakwad

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Cheeky from Suzie Bates! On a length, around middle and leg. Bates shuffles and gets inside the line of the ball to lap it past short fine leg for a boundary.
Short and wide, cutaway to deep point for one.
This is flighted again, well outside off. Bates gets beaten in flight as she looks to go over extra cover. Bates slices it agonizingly past the fielder at backward point and picks up a couple.
On middle, Kerr gives the charge and lifts it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Nicely flighted, outside off. Kerr fetches it and slog-sweeps it away, hard and low into the square leg fence.
Tossed up, around off. Kerr steps out and blocks it away.

DROPPED! Deepti Sharma comes in and creates an opportunity to get rid of the dangerous Suzie Bates off the very first ball but Rajeshwari Gayakwad has spilled the catch. Tossed up, on off. Bates looks to swing across the line but gets a top edge on it around the mid-wicket region. Gaikwad settles under it but the ball goes straight through her clutches. Single taken and Deepti Sharma cannot believe it.
Deepti Sharma comes into the attack now.
Nicely flighted, around off. Kerr defends it out.
On off, driven through extra cover for a run.
Tossed up, on middle and leh. This is flicked towards mid-wicket.
Flighted this time, on off. Bates steps out of her crease and defends it out.
Loppy delivery, on off. Kerr dances down the track and pushes it through mid on for a single.
FOUR! Deft touch! Quicker and flatter, close to the off stump. Amelia Kerr hangs back and uses the pace of the ball to cut it late, past short third man and into the fence.
Rajeshwari Gayakwad is brought into the attack now.
On off, pushed towards mid on.
FOUR! Unlucky! Vastrakar gets the wide yorker in perfectly but Bates manages to squeeze it fine. The ball races away into the third man fence.
FOUR! And again! This time on the other side though. Full, on off and drilled back past the bowler for a boundary down to long off.
FOUR! Full and straight, Bates drives it through mid on and manages to beat long on to pick up a boundary.
Full again and this time the ball is crunched straight to the fielder at extra cover.
Full and wide, pushed towards covers.
Amelia Kerr is in at number 3. Also, Pooja Vastrakar is into the attack now.

OUT! TAKEN! This is a special, special catch by Smriti Mandhana! Length this time, width on offer and Sophie Devine's eyes lit up as she went for the slash. She gets a good connection on it and the ball seems to be flying past point but Smriti Mandhana springs to her left and pouches the catch. Renuka Singh has struck and India can breathe a bit now.
Commentary.Howout: c Smriti Mandhana b Renuka Singh

Commentary.Commentary: Full and wide, steered past point for a single.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries again! On the pads, Bates looks to paddle this one but gets a top edge which flies over backward square leg and runs away into the fence.
FOUR! This is a bit fuller, on middle. Suzie Bates goes for the big heave leg side and almost clears the cow corner fence. The ball goes one bounce into the fence and New Zealand Women flying here.
Full and straight, driven straight to mid on.
A length ball, close to the off pole. Bates waits for it and just opens the face of the bat to guide it towards third man for a couple.
FOUR! Make it three boundaries in the over! Pitched up again, around off. Sophie Devine hangs back and thumps it right back over the bowler's head for back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! Too straight again from Meghna Singh and Devine doesn't let her off the hook. Around middle and this is swung away through mid-wicket for another boundary.
Angling into middle and leg and this is flicked away leg side but not in the gap.
FOUR! Brute force from Sophie Devine this time! Pitched up, right in the slot and Devine hammers it through wide mid on for a boundary.
Nice shape on this one. This is wide outside off and shaping away. Devine goes chasing after it but fails to connect.
Brilliant stop by Smriti Mandhana! A tad bit short and wide, Devine thumps it to the right of point but Mandhana springs that way and saves a certain boundary.
Fuller this time, around off. Driven nicely but straight to covers.
Leg bye! Sliding down the leg side, Devine misses the flick. The ball goes off the pads towards short fine leg and they get a leg bye.
FOUR! Top shot from Sophie Devine! Around off but there's not much width on offer. Devine hangs back and punches it out through covers for another boundary.
Length again, around the top of off. Devine hangs back and defends it out.
Close to the off pole. Bates dabs it down towards point for a quick single.
That is crunched to deep cover! Singh bowls it wider and Devine slaps it towards the fielder in the deep for a single.
FOUR! Width on offer and this is punished! Full and wide, Bates slashes this one over point and the ball flies away into the fence.
Edged away! Length again, outside off. Bates goes hard at it and gets a thick outside edge down towards third man. The batters manage to come back for the second. Excellent running.
Good running! Full and on off. Devine punches it straight to mid off and sets off for the single.
A bit fuller and wider outside off. Devine throws her hands at it and slices it down to the third man region for a couple.
On a good length, around off. This is driven towards the cover region.
Short of a length, pushed well outside off. Devine has to reach out and can't pierce the infield on the off side.
Nicely bowled! Length again, bowled from wider of the crease and jagging back in sharply off the surface. Bates blocks it out.
Skiddish length, around off. Bates taps it towards the cover region.
Wide of off stump, this is steered through cover-point for a single.
That made a cracking sound off the bat! Full, around off and Devine leans in to play the cover drive. The fielder at extra cover gets a hand on it and saves a couple of runs for her side.
On off, pushed towards covers.
A length ball, outside off and there's just a hint of away movement. Devine looks to cut but misses.
Who will bowl from the other end? It;s going to be Renuka Singh.
This is banged in short, on off. Bates gets right on top of the bounce and pulls it down to deep square leg for a couple.
A length ball, around off and this is driven towards point for one.
Lovely shape this time around for Singh. Full, on middle and shaping away. Devine keeps it out.
FOUR! Easy pickings! A juicy full toss, angling down leg. Devine clips it past square leg and picks up another boundary.
FOUR! Sophie Devine and New Zealand Women are underway! A fullish delivery, around off. Devine stands tall and creams it through covers to get up and running with a boundary.
Singh starts off with a back of a length ball, outside off. Devine hangs back and taps it towards point.

We are ready for play! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the India Women players. Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates are set to open the innings for New Zealand Women. Meghna Singh has been handed the new ball and she is raring to go. Let's play...

Suzie Bates says that they are happy to have won the series and did celebrate the win because it hasn't been easy off-late. Now they need to turn their focus onto this match and keep that consistency going, this is also something they have been looking for for quite a while now. She informs that they have a few forced changes to the playing XI.

Mithali Raj says that they will bowl first due to the rain around and the conditions will get better for batting later on. She adds that they are looking forward to winning this match and hoping for an improvement in the overall performance. She also mentions that they need to improve with the ball because they have been batting well in the last couple of matches. Informs that indeed Smriti Mandhana is going to feature today and there are as many as 6 changes to the side.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana (IN FOR Sabbhineni Meghana), Shafali Verma, Yastika Bhatia, Mithali Raj (C), Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh (WK) (IN FOR Taniya Bhatia), Sneh Rana, Pooja Vastrakar (IN FOR Harmanpreet Kaur), Meghna Singh (IN FOR Jhulan Goswami), Rajeshwari Gayakwad (IN FOR Ekta Bisht) and Renuka Singh.

New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Sophie Devine (C), Suzie Bates, Amelia Kerr, Amy Satterthwaite, Frances Mackay, Lauren Down, Katey Martin (WK), Hayley Jensen (IN FOR MADDY GREEN), Hannah Rowe, Jess Kerr (IN FOR LEA TAHUHU) and Rosemary Mair.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and it lands in the favour of India Women. They will have a BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Craig McMillan is alongside Grant Elliott for the pitch report. Craig says that the covers have been on and off throughout the day and that might affect the pitch. Elliott adds that there is a green tinge but it is good for batting. The bowlers might have success early on and the right decision after winning the toss would be to bowl first. They also mention that the boundaries have been brought in today.

UPDATE 0715 IST (0145 GMT) - We have the news all fans have been waiting for! The umpires have made the call and there will be a 20-over game starting at 0810 IST (0240 GMT) with toss being held at 0740 IST(0210 GMT).

UPDATE 0640 IST (0110 GMT) - Excellent news for all the fans out there. The rain has stopped completely and the covers are also coming off. The umpires have scheduled another inspection at 0710 IST (0140 GMT). There are a few wet patches on the field because it's been raining cats and dogs out there but if there's no more rain then we should be able to get in a 20-over game starting at 0810 IST (0240 GMT). Fingers crossed.

UPDATE 0615 IST (0045 GMT) - Well, well. It looks like weather conditions have improved. It is just a light drizzle at the moment and the umpires are out for an inspection. We are waiting for an official word as the cut-off for this game is 0810 IST (0240 GMT) and if we get lucky, we might get a reduced game after all. Fingers crossed. The umpires will have another inspection in about 15 minutes, at 0630 IST (0100 GMT) and the sun is just peeping through the clouds as well.

UPDATE 0531 IST (0001 GMT) - The rain has slowed down but the groundsmen continue to do the hard work of clearing the water from over the cover. The forecast doesn't have anything good to offer on the table. All we can do is hope to see some action before it gets too late. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE 0510 IST (2340 GMT, previous day) - So, the skies did clear up for a while and things looked promising but unfortunately, it's gotten gloomy again and the rain is back. Let's hope that things get promising again and we can have some cricketing action post Lunch. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE 0425 IST (2255 GMT, previous day) - The latest update from the ground is that there is a bit of rain still around and the umpires have decided to take an early Lunch break. They will inspect the ground after Lunch.

UPDATE 0350 IST (2220 GMT, previous day) - The news from the ground is that the rain is persistent at the moment and the forecast for the day ahead doesn't look good either. It has been gloomy weather in the region for the last couple of days but let's hope we get some play in.

Team Update - While we wait for the rain to stop, here's some team news coming out of the White Ferns camp. Batter Brooke Halliday has been ruled out of the remaining couple of ODIs after coming in close contact with a Covid-19 case. While Halliday herself has tested negative, regulations require her to remain isolated for the next seven days.

UPDATE 0305 IST (2135 GMT, previous day) - Right then, the news from the middle is that the toss has been delayed due to rain. It is not heavy but the covers are staying on for the moment. Stay tuned for further updates.

New Zealand White Ferns have scored 270 plus in all of the three ODIs so far and on two of those occasions, they chased down a big target with about an over to go. So it has been a closely fought contest in the last couple of matches but the hosts have been able to manage their nerves better. Amelia Kerr has been brilliant with the bat and with the World Cup looming large, the hosts will look to keep on winning. So, will the visitors finally be able to get over the line? Or will the hosts keep piling on the misery? We'll find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

India have not won a single match in this tour so far but given their improving performances, their chances of winning a game are getting much stronger. Two matches to go, and with the World Cup around the corner, momentum will be a telling factor if India manage to end the series 2-3. They have bettered their performance from the previous match throughout the tour but it just hasn't been enough against the hosts who have been superb with the bat. Smriti Mandhana might finally make an appearance which will only strengthen the batting further. The visitors though need to improve their bowling in the final 10 overs if they are to get a win.

Hello and a warm welcome to the 4th ODI between New Zealand Women and India Women. New Zealand White Ferns have already sealed the 5-match series and have an unassailable lead here. They will be looking to continue the winning momentum whereas India Women will be looking to get over the line and get their first win of the tour.
... MATCH DAY ...
